claims.text: An ALD-grown aluminum oxide coating can enhance the oxidation resistance of a metal substrate.
The aluminum oxide coating provides a protective barrier that limits oxygen diffusion.
The initial metal substrate is prone to oxidation at high temperatures.
ALD can deposit a thin, conformal Al2O3 coating on the substrate.
The intervention produces a continuous, defect-minimized aluminum oxide layer.
The ALD-grown aluminum oxide layer reduces substrate oxidation kinetics by impeding oxygen diffusion.
The conformality of the ALD coating ensures complete coverage of complex geometries.
Under identical high-temperature oxidative conditions, the ALD-coated substrate will have a significantly lower oxidation rate than an uncoated substrate.
An uncoated metal substrate exposed to high temperature and oxygen undergoes rapid oxidation and degradation.
Mechanical stress may create coating defects that limit oxidation protection.
Operating above the stability range of the deposited Al2O3 film may limit the method's effectiveness.
The optimal ALD film thickness and deposition temperature are not established by the provided evidence.
The method's performance across varied real-world conditions is not established by the provided evidence.
